=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text minus "-"
text tred "red"
text twhite "white"
text tblue "blue"
text tok "in flag order: "
text tyes "yes\n"
text tno "no\n"
global vals long 16
global seed ulong 1
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note rnd is Knuth's MMIX linear congruential generator, x = x*6364136223846793005 + 1442695040888963407
note mod 2^64 (ulong arithmetic wraps), starting from seed 0; it returns the top 31 bits, x >> 33
fn rnd to ulong
x = add mul get seed 0 6364136223846793005 1442695040888963407
put seed 0 x
ret shr x 33
end
fn ball c long to void
if eq c 0
emit tred
end
if eq c 1
emit twhite
end
if eq c 2
emit tblue
end
end
fn show n ulong to void
for i ulong n
if gt i 0
emit sp
end
ball get vals i
end
emit nl
end
fn inorder n ulong to bool
for i ulong sub n 1
if gt get vals i get vals add i 1
ret false
end
end
ret true
end
fn swap i ulong j ulong to void
t = get vals i
put vals i get vals j
put vals j t
end
note Dijkstra's three-way partition: [0,lo) red, [lo,mid) white, (hi,n) blue; every pass moves mid up
note or hi down, so n passes suffice
fn flag n ulong to void
lo = ulong 0
mid = ulong 0
hi = n
while lt mid hi bound 16
c = get vals mid
if eq c 0
swap lo mid
lo = add lo 1
mid = add mid 1
else
if eq c 1
mid = add mid 1
else
hi = sub hi 1
swap mid hi
end
end
end
end
note draws 12 random balls (0 red, 1 white, 2 blue), drawing again while they happen to be in order;
note with this generator the first draw is already out of order, and 100 draws bound it
fn main to int
n = ulong 12
while true bound 100
for i ulong n
put vals i long rem rnd 3
end
if not inorder n
break
end
end
show n
emit tok
if inorder n
emit tyes
else
emit tno
end
flag n
show n
emit tok
if inorder n
emit tyes
else
emit tno
end
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
blue red white white blue blue blue blue red red white red
in flag order: no
red red red red white white white blue blue blue blue blue
in flag order: yes
</pre>
